title: Condensed local Frobenius trace is invariant under one Frobenius translate
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $k$ be a field of positive prime characteristic $p\ne\ell$, put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and let $X$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $\underline\Omega=\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$ and $\mathcal D_T=D^b_c(T)[[\underline\Omega]]$ for $T=X,s$, with coefficient pullback, module-object derived pullbacks and tensor products [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible, def-sfb-dc-upper-star, def-sfb-dc-tensor]. Let $\Psi:X\to X$ be any $k$-endomorphism and let $M\in\mathcal D_X$ have an isomorphism $\psi:L\Psi^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Define $\psi_0$ by identity pullback and $\psi_{r+1}=\psi\circ L\Psi^*(\psi_r)$ using the canonical identity and pullback-composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback], so $\psi_r:L(\Psi^r)^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Fix $m\geq0$ and a $k$-point $z:s\to X$ with $\Psi^m z=z$. For any $\Psi^m$-fixed point $t$, define $V_{t,m}:Lt^*M\to Lt^*M$ as the canonical fixed-point pullback identification $Lt^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lt^*L(\Psi^m)^*M$ followed by $Lt^*(\psi_m)$; these are the stalkFrobenius operators. Then $\Psi z$ is also fixed by $\Psi^m$. If $Lz^*M$ and $L(\Psi z)^*M$ have right duals in $\mathcal D_s$, their categorical traces [sk-d-trace] satisfy
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(V_{\Psi z,m})=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(V_{z,m})\quad\text{in }\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal D_s}(U_s),$$
where $U_s$ is the coefficient unit. No finite-field model, finite fixed-point set, integral lattice, or global trace identity is assumed.

source.place: Part (3), commuting iterated Weil maps: condensed-module-object analogue stated and proved in the live project, lean/WeilConjectures/TraceFormula/Slop/Stalk.lean:238–250, AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.CondensedRing.WeilBoundedConstructible.trace_stalkFrobenius_comp; this coefficient analogue is not a verbatim statement of the finite-coefficient blueprint

proof.text: Write $F=\Psi$ and $z_j=F^j\circ z$ for $j\geq0$. Associativity gives $F^m\circ z_j=F^j\circ F^m\circ z=z_j$, so every $z_j$ is fixed by $F^m$, including $z_1=\Psi z$. Also $z_{m+j}=z_j$ as actual morphisms $s\to X$. No finiteness or invertibility of $F$ is used.

source.place: Part (3), the loop based at a fixed point; elementary equality of powers of the single endomorphism.

proof.text: Put $B_j=Lz_j^*M$. Let $c_j:Lz_{j+1}^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz_j^*LF^*M$ be the pullback-composition comparison, and set $A_j=(Lz_j^*\psi)\circ c_j:B_{j+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_j$. The cited coherence theorem supplies the module-object and derived composition comparisons and their identity, associativity and common-composite compatibilities; it applies to the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring used here. Functors preserve inverses, so $A_j$ is an isomorphism. Substituting the morphism equality $z_{m+j}=z_j$ identifies $B_{m+j}$ with $B_j$ and $A_{m+j}$ with $A_j$: both the functor $Lz_j^*$ and its natural comparison $c_j$ then have identical arguments. In particular $A_m=A_0$ after these equality identifications.

source.place: Part (2), canonical pullback-stalk comparisons; Part (3), the one-step transport. Coherence is taken from the cited node, not from finite-coefficient stalk comparisons.

proof.text: For $j,r\geq0$, let $C_{j,r}:B_{j+r}\to B_j$ be $Lz_j^*\psi_r$ preceded by $Lz_{j+r}^*M\cong Lz_j^*L(F^r)^*M$. Prove simultaneously for all $j$ by induction on $r$ that $C_{j,0}=1_{B_j}$ and, for $r>0$, $C_{j,r}=A_j\circ A_{j+1}\circ\cdots\circ A_{j+r-1}$. The base follows from the identity comparison and $\psi_0=1$. For the successor, substitute $\psi_{r+1}=\psi\circ LF^*\psi_r$; naturality of the composition comparison moves $Lz_j^*LF^*\psi_r$ past $c_j$, and the associativity comparison identifies the remaining pullback from $z_j,F,F^r$ with that from $z_{j+1},F^r$. Thus $C_{j,r+1}=A_j\circ C_{j+1,r}$, which gives the displayed product by the induction hypothesis. For $r=m$, the equality $z_{j+m}=z_j$ and the identity coherence show from the definition of the fixed-point identification that $C_{j,m}=V_{z_j,m}$.

source.place: Parts (2)–(3), expand the iterated Weil map and the commuting-iterate cocycle as an explicit induction on the length of the stalk path.

proof.text: If $m=0$, step 3 gives $V_{z,0}=1_{B_0}$ and $V_{z_1,0}=1_{B_1}$, hence $A_0\circ V_{z_1,0}=V_{z,0}\circ A_0$. If $m>0$, step 3 and $A_m=A_0$ give $A_0\circ V_{z_1,m}=A_0\circ A_1\circ\cdots\circ A_m=(A_0\circ\cdots\circ A_{m-1})\circ A_0=V_{z,m}\circ A_0$. This is associativity of composition of the displayed maps, not an identification of arbitrary coefficient categories. Since $A_0$ is invertible it conjugates $V_{z_1,m}$ to $V_{z,m}$.

source.place: Part (3), the two routes around the stalk loop, with the actual maps and the zero-iterate case written out.

proof.text: Apply the cited categorical conjugacy theorem in the braided (indeed symmetric) monoidal category $\mathcal D_s$ with $P=B_1$, $Q=B_0$, $u=V_{z_1,m}$, $v=V_{z,m}$ and $a=A_0$. The two required right duals are exactly those assumed in the item; step 4 is its intertwining hypothesis. Its conclusion is $\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(V_{\Psi z,m})=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathcal D_s}(V_{z,m})$ as endomorphisms of the same unit $U_s$.

source.place: Part (3), last sentence, using the abstract categorical conjugacy law rather than the perfect ordinary-module specialization.
